# Best MagSafe (Qi2) car mounts

There isn't one winner. The right pick depends on your phone, your vents, and how much you want to spend.

**Best for most iPhone drivers: Belkin BoostCharge Qi2 15W vent mount, $47.99**
- Three of the roundups ([RottenWiFi](https://rottenwifi.com/best-magsafe-car-mounts-in-2026-connect-charge-and-drive/), [iTechGuides](https://www.itechguides.com/best-magsafe-car-mounts-in-2026-connect-charge-and-drive/), [CloudsPress](https://www.cloudspress.com/best-magsafe-car-mounts-in-2026-connect-charge-and-drive/)) pick it as best overall. They appear to be near-identical articles, so treat them as one opinion rather than three.
- It comes with a 27W car adapter and a 1 m USB-C cable, and rotates between portrait and landscape.
- It fits cases up to 3 mm thick.
- It needs vent slats no thicker than 3 mm and no deeper than 20 mm. Straight horizontal slats work best, and vertical ones may droop.
- If your vents are awkward, Belkin also makes a vent/dash version at the same price.

**Best for fastest charging and reliability: Anker Prime Qi2 25W (AirCool), $89.99**
- Mount Guys uses it as their [daily driver](https://www.mountguys.com/best-magsafe-car-mount/) and calls it best overall. [The Gadgeteer](https://the-gadgeteer.com/2026/06/16/best-magsafe-car-mounts-iphone-2026/) lists it at $69.99 on sale, down from $89.99.
- It has active cooling (thermoelectric plus a fan), which helps keep the phone from throttling when it's running navigation in the sun.
- It charges at up to 25W on the iPhone 17 and 16 Pro Max/Plus, but only 22W on the iPhone 16 and 16 Pro, 20W on the iPhone Air, and 15W on iPhone 15 and earlier.
- It needs a 45W+ USB-C car adapter. Mount Guys and The Gadgeteer say a 60W adapter is in the box, but the other roundups don't mention one, so check the listing before buying.
- Anker lists it as incompatible with Tesla and Mercedes-Benz vents.

**Best value with a fan: ESR HaloLock 15W with CryoBoost**
- It's Qi2-certified and has a cooling fan. You can mount it on a vent or the dash with the included 3M adhesive.
- ESR's store price is $39.99, and code PARTNER18 brought it to $32.80 when tested on Oct 22. [Buy at ESR](https://dealectric.com/go/esr-halolock-15w-wireless-car-charger-cryoboost). This is an affiliate link, so Dealectric earns a commission at no cost to you.
- It comes with a 30-day return window and a 12-month warranty.
- The listing doesn't say whether a car adapter is included, and The Gadgeteer says an 18W adapter isn't. Budget $10–15 for one.
- Prices vary a lot between sources (The Gadgeteer lists $35.99 in one place and $18.99 in another), so check the final price at checkout.

**Other options**
- **LISEN Qi2.2 25W with fan, about $39.95:** It's the best-overall pick in [The Gadgeteer's roundup](https://the-gadgeteer.com/2026/06/16/best-magsafe-car-mounts-iphone-2026/) and comes with a 95W adapter. It uses a large suction-cup base, and the fan must stay on to reach 25W.
- **PITAKA MagEZ Car Mount Pro 2, $59.99:** It has a nice design and an NFC Shortcuts trigger, but no fan, so it may throttle on hot dashboards.
- **VICSEED steel-core vent mount (no charging):** Mount Guys recommends it as a simple, sturdy backup. It's a researched pick, not hands-on tested.

**Before you buy**
1. Check your vent style (see the Belkin and Anker limits above). If it's a poor fit, choose a dash or suction mount.
2. For 25W charging you need both a 25W-capable iPhone and a 45W+ car adapter. Otherwise a 15W Qi2 mount is enough.
3. Look for a real Qi2 badge. "MagSafe-compatible" alone may mean only 7.5W.
4. Ignore big "suction pounds" or "gf" claims. They often describe the dash suction cup, not the phone grip.

I can't open the store pages from here, so I couldn't confirm current stock or exact prices for Belkin or Anker. Those roundups' Amazon buttons are the quickest way to check. If you tell me your phone model and car, I can narrow this to one pick.
